content.thinking:
I'm tracing the failure: account pages broke for many shoppers, and the requests hit a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py at line 47.

I'm checking whether a deploy could explain it, and the records show no deploy came back in the window, with all three replicas on one revision. I'm also noting the flag was off during 21:03–21:32 while normal pages were served, so the switch lines up with the errors.

I'm weighing whether a client disconnect could account for the errors, but those showed up before the flag flipped at 21:33 and at a normal baseline rate, so they look like background noise. The flag was switched on at 21:33 and everything after that lines up with it. The actual mechanism I can confirm is the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47, though the logs don't yet show why the divisor ends up zero.

Now I'm weighing the contributing factors, starting with the flag being switched on for all production traffic at once, with no staged rollout or check visible in the records.

I'm working through the contributing factors now: the flag went live for all production traffic at once, with no staged rollout or guard visible in the records, and I'm weighing how a small share first with an automatic error-rate check would have caught this sooner. I'm also noting that no test seems to have exercised the spend-summary path with the zero-divisor data, so requiring coverage for flagged code paths before enablement looks like the gap to close.

I'm now sketching action items, starting with a fix for the division at spend_summary.py:47 so a zero divisor no longer fails account pages, paired with a test that covers that case.

I'm now sorting out the action items: a fix for the division at spend_summary.py:47 that stops a zero divisor from failing account pages, plus a requirement that code behind a feature flag is tested with the flag on before it can be enabled in production. I'm still weighing whether to add a separate step to find which requests send a zero divisor into that line.

I'm settling on the action items now: a fix so a zero divisor at spend_summary.py:47 no longer fails account pages, a regression test for that case, and a process rule that code behind a feature flag gets tested with the flag on before it's enabled. I'm also considering keeping the monthly-spend feature off until the fix is merged.

I'm wrapping up the action items and noting the flag stays off until the fix ships, so turning it back on can't fail account pages again. Then I'm listing what went well: the investigator placed the start at the flag change, the mitigation turned the flag off, and the team kept it off and paged checkout.

I'm weighing what went well and what didn't, and I'm noting that the response itself went without anything clearly going wrong. Then I'm looking at the assumptions: the ZeroDivisionError lines are being treated as the failures behind the error rate rise, though the log lines are sampled and the error rate is a separate measure. I'm also flagging that whether turning the flag off actually ended the failures hasn't been measured.

I'm writing up the root cause now: turning on the monthly-spend feature routes account page requests through the spend-summary code, which raises an unhandled ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47 for some requests. The record doesn't yet show why the divisor comes out as zero.

I'm checking the chain of evidence now: the failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47, and that code only ran because the monthly-spend flag was on.

I'm checking whether a deploy could explain the failures: no deploy came back from the day before, and the account pages were rendering normally before the onset with the current revision in place.

I'm checking the chain step by step: account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47, and I'm ruling out other causes by confirming no deploy came back from the day before and that the only flag change in the hour was this one. The code behind that flag is what divides by a zero value for some account requests.

I'm checking the remaining steps of the causal chain now, and I'm reviewing the flag-on path and the line-47 division to confirm they explain the failure. I'm also settling on the framing for the contributing factors.

action_items.item: Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so that a zero divisor no longer fails the account page request.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix to src/io_shop/spend_summary.py is merged and deployed.
Roll out feature flags in production to a small share of traffic first, and turn the flag off automatically if the error rate rises after the change.
Require that code behind a feature flag is tested with the flag on, including edge-case account data such as zero values, before the flag can be switched on in production.

causal_chain.step: The requests failed with a ZeroDivisionError raised at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, starting in the minute the incident began. Before that minute, the only account-page failures logged were shoppers closing the connection.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or a revision change: no deploy came back from the window that was read, the flag change was the only production change read back, and account pages rendered normally with the running revision in place before the onset.
A different flag change: the flag provider's history showed only this one flag change by anyone other than Argus in the hour that was read.
Shoppers closing their connections: these errors were logged while the service ran normally before the onset, and stopped being logged before it.

causal_chain.step: That code ran because admin switched the monthly-spend-feature flag on at {P1.1}. The flag read off on every evaluation before that minute, was split between off and on during that minute, and read on for every evaluation after it.
The code path behind the flag divides by a value that is zero for some account page requests, and the failure takes down the whole page request.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature sent account pages through new code that divided by zero for some shoppers, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag was switched from off for all traffic to on for all traffic within a single minute. No staged rollout, and no automatic check of the error rate tied to the flag change, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: If the flag had been turned on for a small share of shoppers first, with an automatic error-rate check, only that share would have hit the failure, and the flag could have been turned back off before most account pages were affected.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test or pre-enablement check was seen that ran the spend-summary path with the flag on against account data that gives a zero divisor.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a test would have raised the ZeroDivisionError before the flag was switched on in production, and the flag would have stayed off until the code was fixed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident in the same minute as the flag change.
The Investigator Agent formed a single candidate cause that named the flag change and the ZeroDivisionError in the logs.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back off. The action can be undone.
Some Person kept the flag off and paged the checkout team.

input.root_cause: The spend-summary code that monthly-spend-feature turns on raises a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 for some account page requests, and nothing catches the error, so the whole account page request fails. The evidence does not show why the divisor is zero for those requests.
input.still_at_risk: If anyone switches monthly-spend-feature back on before the spend-summary code is fixed, account pages could fail the same way again.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
